summary.text: A 35-year-old woman presented with blurred vision and photopsia in both eyes for 3 months and had been treated with oral prednisone at 30 mg per day for over 6 years for nephritic syndrome. Her BCVA was 20/63 in each eye, and the left eye had a focal retinal pigment epithelial detachment in the inferior retina.

Ophthalmoscopy, B scan, FFA and OCT of the right eye showed bullous retinal detachment in the posterior pole, hyperfluorescent leakage and neuro-retinal detachment, and ICGA showed hyperfluorescent leakage of the choroid. The right eye received a 50% dose of verteporfin PDT with a 5000 μm spot.

One month later the SRF was partly reduced, and at 3 months there was retinal reattachment with complete absence of SRF. At 6 months the right-eye BCVA was 20/50 with a mottled fundus, no fluorescein leakage and ICGA hypofluorescence in the lesion area; no recurrence or major sequelae occurred.

summary.text: A 35-year-old man first noted visual loss in both eyes, was diagnosed with classic central serous chorioretinopathy and received argon laser photocoagulation in the right eye at another hospital. Two years later, at the age of 37, he had severe blurring in the left eye, with BCVA 20/80 in the right eye and 20/200 in the left eye.

Ophthalmoscopy, B scan, FFA, OCT and ICGA of the left eye showed exudative lesions, bullous retinal detachment, hyperfluorescent leakage, SRF, sub-retinal fibrin and retinal folds. The left eye received a 50% dose of verteporfin PDT with two spots of 6000 and 3000 μm.

One month after PDT the SRF decreased and sub-retinal fibrin disappeared. At 3 months the retina was reattached with complete SRF resolution and no hyperfluorescent leakage. At 6 months BCVA improved to 20/40 and remained stable; no recurrence or major sequelae occurred.

summary.text: A 38-year-old man had a history of blurred vision in the right eye for 1 year and CSC in the left eye treated with argon laser photocoagulation 10 years ago. His BCVA was 20/63 in the right eye and 20/200 in the left eye.

Right-eye ophthalmoscopy, B scan, FFA and OCT showed retinal detachment with fibrinoid exudative lesions, bullous detachment, hyperfluorescent leakages, severe SRF and sub-retinal fibrin. A 50% dose of verteporfin PDT with three spots was given; SRF resolved slowly until the second month, so a second 50% PDT with a 5000 μm spot was given.

One month after the second PDT the retina was reattached and SRF markedly decreased; SRF was nearly resolved at 2 months and completely resolved at 3 months. Table 1 gives 20/20 at the 6th month, and no recurrence or major sequelae occurred.

summary.text: A 48-year-old man presented with blurred vision in the left eye for 2 weeks. He had a history of intravitreal triamcinolone acetonide injection for a misdiagnosis of uveitis 1 month prior to examination, and further injections and laser at another hospital brought no improvement of visual acuity; BCVA was 20/20 in the right eye and 20/200 in the left.

Ophthalmoscopy, B scan, FFA and OCT showed intraocular TA, non-rhegmatogenous retinal detachment with multifocal exudative lesions, bullous retinal detachment, hyperfluorescent leakages and SRF. The left eye received a 50% dose of verteporfin PDT with two spots of 5000 μm and one spot of 3000 μm.

One month later the bullous detachment and SRF were reduced; at 3 months the retina was reattached, SRF had disappeared and FFA and ICGA showed hypofluorescence in the lesion area. At 6 months BCVA was 20/100 in the left eye, and no recurrence occurred.

summary.text: A 50-year-old man presented with blurred vision in the right eye for a year. His BCVA was 20/200 in the right eye, and the left eye had worsened to no light perception because of glaucoma at an early age.

Ophthalmoscopy showed non-rhegmatogenous retinal detachment in the posterior pole and B scan confirmed bullous retinal detachment; FFA showed hyperfluorescent leakages around the optic disc, and OCT showed serious SRF, sub-retinal fibrin and retinal folds. Five spots of 50% verteporfin PDT were administered under ICGA guidance.

One month after PDT the detachment, SRF and fibrin had decreased and the retinal folds had disappeared. At 3 months the bullous detachment had resolved with retinal reattachment, no fluorescein leakage and complete resolution of SRF and fibrin on OCT. BCVA improved to 20/40 with no recurrence during more than 6 months.

Case 3 first-session BCVA 20/25 sits in a sentence whose 1-month time attaches to the B scan finding, so its time is left null.
